title: Getting work trucks and fleet vans ready for salt season
description: Salt, brine and slush are back on Calgary roads. How to prep work trucks and fleet vans now, and keep cabs and paint in shape until spring.
excerpt: November is when brine, gravel and wet boots start doing damage to trucks that work every day. What to do now, what to schedule through winter, and why on-site service fits fleets.
imageAlt: Pickup truck cab floor cleaned during an on-site work truck detail in Calgary

sections.heading: Why early November matters for trucks that work
paragraphs: By now most Calgary-area crews have seen the first snow, the first round of road brine and the first week of slush tracked into every cab. For a personal car that is a nuisance. For a pickup or van that runs Deerfoot, Stoney Trail and job sites from Airdrie to Okotoks every day, it is the start of five months of steady wear.

The easiest time to get ahead of it is before the buildup starts. A truck that goes into winter clean and protected is far easier to keep presentable than one that is already carrying a layer of last week's salt.

sections.heading: What winter does to the cab
paragraphs: Most of the damage in a work truck happens on the floor. Wet boots carry in slush, gravel and salt, and once the water dries the salt stays behind as white crust in the carpet and on the mats. Left long enough, it stiffens the fibres and is much harder to lift out.

Grit also gets ground into seat fabric every time someone climbs in with dirty workwear. Add coffee spills, fogged-up glass and a dash that gets touched with gloves all day, and a cab can look rough by January even if the truck itself is in good condition.

A pre-winter interior clean resets all of that. Carpets and mats are shampooed or extracted, salt and mud stains are worked out, seats are cleaned, and the dash, console, vents and door panels are degreased so the cab starts the season from a clean baseline.

sections.heading: What winter does to the outside
paragraphs: Brine and salt cling to lower panels, wheels, arches and running boards, which are exactly the areas that get the least attention between washes. Road film builds up on the glass and makes night driving harder now that the commute is mostly in the dark.

A proper hand wash that gets into the wheels, arches, running boards and the box and tailgate takes that buildup off instead of moving it around. If you want an extra layer between the paint and the brine, a ceramic sealant can be added to a detail so water and slush release more easily through the season.

sections.heading: One truck or a whole fleet
paragraphs: For an owner-operator or a small business running one or two trucks, our Work Truck Package is built for this. It comes as interior only or interior plus exterior, and covers the clean-out, carpet and mat extraction, salt stain removal and a full exterior wash. Details and current pricing are on the detailing page.

For companies with five or more units, a scheduled fleet rotation usually makes more sense. We walk the fleet, set a service level per vehicle type and agree on a schedule. Over winter, that schedule can be tighter on the vehicles that see the most slush and site traffic and looser on the rest.

sections.heading: Why on-site service fits winter fleet work
paragraphs: Every hour a truck sits at a wash bay or a shop is an hour it is not on a job. We come to your yard, shop or lot across Calgary, Airdrie, Cochrane, Chestermere, Okotoks and Rocky View County, and our self-contained vans carry their own water and power.
Fleet work can be scheduled early, late or on weekends so vehicles are not pulled off shift, and fleet accounts get a single monthly invoice with a per-unit breakdown.

sections.heading: Simple habits between visits
paragraphs: Rubber floor liners make the biggest difference, since salt and slush stay in the tray instead of soaking into carpet. Knock boots off before climbing in, empty the liners when they fill, and keep a soft brush in the truck for the seats. Rinsing the lower body and wheels on milder days also keeps brine from sitting on the same panels for weeks.

faqs.q: Can salt stains be removed from truck carpets?
faqs.a: In most cases, yes. Salt stain removal and carpet and mat extraction are part of the Work Truck Package. Stains that have been left for a long time may take more work, and we will tell you what to expect before starting.

faqs.q: Do you need access to water or power at our yard?
faqs.a: No. Our vans are self-contained, so we can work in a yard, lot or job site without using your water or power.
Fleet work is quoted per unit after we see the vehicles, based on type, condition and frequency. For one or two trucks, the Work Truck Package pricing is listed on the detailing page.
